description: Apple announces Memory Integrity Enforcement with the iPhone 17 and iPhone Air, naming the A19 and A19 Pro chips.
usbliter8 BootROM exploit for A12 and A13 devices is publicised (reported by secondary outlets and a national CERT).
Dopamine 3.0 released; secondary coverage quotes a support table of iOS 15.0 to 17.3.1 for A8 to A17 and M1 to M2, and iOS 26.0 to 26.0.1 for A12 and A13.
device_scope: A8 to A17 and M1 to M2 (as quoted)
firmware_scope: iOS 15.0 to 17.3.1 (as quoted); A12 and A13 to 26.0.1

description: iOS 27.0 released (build 24A437 per the third-party index).
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (iPhone16,2) and other iPhones

description: iOS 27.0.1 released (build 24A446). Apple's security releases index lists no published CVE entries for this build.
Calif.io reportedly demonstrates an untethered iOS 27.0.1 jailbreak on an iPhone 18 Pro at Hexacon 2026 in Paris.
Apple's iOS 27 security notes are updated with CVE entries credited to Calif.io researchers, two of them jointly with Claude and Anthropic Research.
firmware_scope: iOS 27 (fixed-in release per CVE not confirmed)

description: Apple's index lists iOS 27.1 for iPhone Duo with no published CVE entries.
iOS 27.2 released (build 24B119 per the third-party index). Secondary press reports 163 fixed vulnerabilities; Apple's 27.2 advisory was not located.
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (iPhone16,2) per the index

description: A community reference states that iOS 27.0.1 was still signed on 2026-11-02. This is not independently verified and conflicts with the third-party index checked on 2026-11-11.
Dopamine 3.0.13 published. Release notes describe a posix_spawn hook fix and a SpringBoard snapshot change. They do not state iOS 27 support.
Press reports that Apple responded to MIE-bypass claims with an iOS update. Details were not verified.
Reported plan for a kernel read/write exploit and write-up from a Calif.io-linked researcher within about a week. Coverage conflicts; no primary announcement was located.
Press coverage through about 2026-11-06 reports that Apple fixed most flaws in iOS 27.2 and that no public tool is planned.
iOS 27.2.1 released (build 24B156 per the third-party index and the Wikipedia infobox).
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (iPhone16,2) per the index

description: Press reports Apple stopped signing iOS 26.6.2 after iOS 27 shipped. Used as a pattern example for how older builds lose signing.
Tracker snapshot. The third-party index lists iOS 27.0.1 as not signed. A community reference reports the opposite for 2026-11-02, so the status is unresolved.
Independent academic analysis of SPTM, TXM and Exclaves (arXiv:2510.09272) is submitted. Its firmware analysis uses iPhone 16 (A18) on iOS 18.4, not the A17 Pro or iOS 27.
device_scope: iPhone 16 (A18) in the paper's firmware analysis

description: An opa334 PSA dated 2026-10-17 is reported by the upstream reference to warn of an SPTM bypass valid through iOS 27.0.1. The original was not located in this review.

Reported (upstream reference, V31): opa334 says Dopamine A12 and A13 support could follow using momentarius once a kernel read/write exploit is public; A14 and later still need an SPTM bypass. Original not retrieved.
device_scope: A12 and A13 (as reported); A14 and later (as reported)

description: Reported (upstream reference, V32): a Calif.io video shows Lockdown Mode, an over-the-air update to iOS 27.2, and a reboot after which a plugin still works. Video and original post not retrieved.
The one-week window reported on 2026-11-04 for a kernel read/write write-up lapses. No publication, repository or source-code release for the announced work was found on 2026-11-12.
Research pass for the v0.2.0 update: Apple's iOS 27.2 and 27.2.1 advisories parsed, the upstream reference reconciled, and the kernel, Calif.io and SPTM evidence re-classified.
Apple's iOS 27 security page is updated with entries marked as added on 2026-10-26, including CVE-2026-112608 (CoreMedia) and CVE-2026-86916 (kernel privilege impact).

Dopamine 3.0 release notes state a Titan PPL/SPTM bypass for iOS 16.5.1 to 17.3.1, a momentarius PPL bypass for A12 and A13, and that real-device SPTM support ends at iOS 17.3.1 because no bypass is known for 17.4 and later.
device_scope: A12 and A13 and SPTM devices (release-note wording)

description: The upstream reference reports a Calif.io team member's interview on end-user tools, the scope of the chain and a 27.2 patch statement. The interview was not retrieved.
device_scope: Not stated (any iPhone running iOS 27.0.1, as reported)

description: A Calif.io social account reportedly posted a bare hash without explanation (upstream reference). The content it commits to is unknown.
A company-branded account reportedly showed a root shell on iOS 27.2 (upstream reference). Single-party, unverified (C-063).

A project announced a semi-untethered iOS 27.0 to 27.0.1 jailbreak with a planned release one to two weeks later (upstream reference). The upstream reference found no proof of concept or third-party validation. No release was reviewed in this pass. Any future release should be treated as potentially malicious (C-064).
device_scope: iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro), as reported as the test device

description: The third-party index lists iOS 27.0.1 (24A446) as not signed on 2026-11-12. The upstream reference recorded it as signed on 2026-11-02. The date of the change is not known (C-021).

Local static provenance and Ghidra analysis of the 24A446 kernelcache and the SPTM and TXM monitor images. Manifest digests match the normal containers; restore-entry digests do not match (unresolved). The complete package was not hashed. Readiness is unchanged.

Static research on the 24A446 kernelcache and monitors: symbolication with a third-party signature set, a KEXT import investigation, monitor structure counts, a memory-protection documentation re-read, and metadata comparison with the 24B119 and 24B156 builds. The v0.3.0 release was not created. Readiness is unchanged.
